chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from Zurarah who said:
I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'Are women subject to the call to prayer (adhan)?' He said: 'When they testify the two declarations of faith, that is sufficient for them.'
ai.seo_question: Are women required to listen to the Adhan in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that the Adhan is not a strict obligation (wajib) for women, distinguishing their religious status from the ritual requirement to hear the call. The Imam asserts that their declaration of the Shahadah is sufficient, reflecting the Shia juristic view that while women are encouraged to attend congregational prayers, the Adhan itself serves primarily as a notification for the general community rather than a binding condition for female validity of prayer.
